open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole.” / “None open.”
open_points.question: Is the reopened State 0 still unaccepted, or do R0-61 to R0-71 constitute acceptance of the revised whole?
options: State 0 remains reopened until a new whole-document acceptance
R0-71 implicitly closes and accepts State 0
Each accepted post-R0-60 decision is authoritative without whole-document acceptance
open_points.default_guess: Treat State 0 as reopened and not yet accepted as a whole.

open_points.subject: Owner authentication
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” and “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session.”
open_points.question: What Registry action lets a browser without an existing session sign in, what observable result does it return, and how are missing or wrong credentials refused without contradicting the rule that no unauthenticated request answers?
options: An unauthenticated sign-in endpoint is an explicit exception
The credential authenticates the sign-in request itself
Authentication is performed by an unnamed system in front of Registry
open_points.default_guess: Treat the credential-bearing sign-in request as authenticated and allow only the sign-in form or challenge before it.

open_points.subject: Test-instance authority
open_points.text: “Test instances — any other instance (the agent's machine, a rig, a developer laptop)” while credentials and administration are described only for the production instance and owner.
open_points.question: Who is allowed to administer and call a test instance, what credentials does it use, and does an agent controlling its own machine act as owner there or remain under agent restrictions?
options: Each test instance has its own owner principal and credentials
Agents may administer test instances but never production
Test instances use the same actor restrictions as production
open_points.default_guess: Give each test instance separate credentials and treat its administrator as that instance's owner, without granting production authority.

open_points.subject: Cabinet Web mirror connectivity
open_points.text: “Consumer services — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, the Cabinet Web mirror” but the service API is “reachable only inside VM Platform and over the WireGuard channel from the VPS.”
open_points.question: Where does the Cabinet Web mirror run, and through which permitted network path can it use its optional token to read Registry?
options: Inside VM Platform
On the VPS over WireGuard
It has no production access and should be removed as a consumer
open_points.default_guess: Assume it runs inside VM Platform.

open_points.subject: Agent projection confidentiality
open_points.text: “never receives a `personal_data` value” versus “Room names and artifact pointers stay in it; the owner names rooms without names or addresses of people, and a producer publishes `uri`, `payload_ref` and digest without them. Registry does not inspect these values.”
open_points.question: How can Registry guarantee that no personal value reaches an agent when agent-visible room names and pointer fields are unrestricted and uninspected, and what failure occurs when a value violates that rule?
options: Registry validates or classifies these values and refuses unsafe ones
Room names and pointer values are removed from the agent projection
The guarantee is weakened to depend on owner and producer discipline
open_points.default_guess: Treat the guarantee as dependent on owner and producer discipline, because Registry explicitly does not inspect the values.

open_points.subject: Anonymised-project contents
open_points.text: “a project's id is not anonymous by itself” and artifact pointers are uninspected, but “An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else” and “It holds no personal value.”
open_points.question: Under what condition can a retained project id and its uninspected pointers be declared non-identifying, and what happens if either still permits re-identification or contains personal data?
options: Anonymisation is refused unless governance establishes that retained values are non-identifying
Pointers and possibly the id are removed when they remain identifying
The claim that an anonymised project holds no personal value is withdrawn
open_points.default_guess: Refuse anonymisation unless the owner has established outside Registry that the retained id and pointers are non-identifying.

open_points.subject: Session-scoped agent operations
open_points.text: “On every agent-authority call Registry checks three things … the session it names is registered; and the `project_id` is in that session's set” and “An agent-authority operation that names no project, in a session with no active project, is refused,” while registration creates a session “with no granted project” and Kernel may then read its access or request access.
open_points.question: Which Kernel operations are session-scoped exceptions that may run without a project in the granted set or an active project?
options: Registration, access read and access request are explicit session-scoped exceptions
Only registration is exempt; access read and request require an active project
R0-53 and R0-69 apply only to project-scoped operations
open_points.default_guess: Apply project membership and active-project checks only to project-scoped operations; exempt registration, access read and access request.

open_points.subject: Session access version
open_points.text: “the access version” and “the context's version” are returned, but no text says what the version means or which accepted actions move it.
open_points.question: Which changes increment the session access version, and what observable use does a caller make of it?
options: Every grant, revoke, active-project change and pending-request change increments it
Only changes to the granted set or active project increment it
It is a concurrency token supplied on session mutations
open_points.default_guess: Increment it for every change to grants, active project or pending request, and use it for stale-change detection.

open_points.subject: Repeated customer-state changes
open_points.text: “restrict or lift a restriction on a customer” and “end or resume a customer relationship” specify only unknown or erased customers as failures.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner restricts an already restricted customer, lifts an unrestricted one, ends an already ended relationship, or resumes one that is not ended; in particular, may a repeated end replace the recorded date?
options: Return the current record unchanged
Refuse an invalid or duplicate transition
Accept repeats and replace applicable dates
open_points.default_guess: Return the current record unchanged and never replace an existing end date on a repeated end.

open_points.subject: Repeated mutations versus stale revisions
open_points.text: “A change against an older revision is refused” versus “archiving an archived project returns it unchanged,” “erasing an erased customer returns it unchanged,” and “anonymising an anonymised project returns it unchanged.”
open_points.question: When an idempotent repeated action carries a stale revision, does stale-revision refusal take precedence, or does the operation return the unchanged current record?
options: Stale revision is always refused first
An already-achieved terminal state returns unchanged despite a stale revision
Each action defines its own precedence
open_points.default_guess: Apply stale-revision refusal before terminal-state idempotency.

open_points.subject: Owner confirmations
open_points.text: Actions name the owner “after confirming” or “confirming,” and audit entries may carry “a confirmation id,” but confirmation itself has no action, output or failure.
open_points.question: What constitutes confirmation for archive, import, project erasure and audit erasure, and what does Registry do when confirmation is absent, stale, for another action or already used?
options: Confirmation is part of the same submitted owner form
Registry issues a separate single-use confirmation id
The protected owner session alone counts as confirmation
open_points.default_guess: Use a same-form confirmation bound to the exact action, target and revision, and refuse missing or mismatched confirmation.

open_points.subject: Answering an access request
open_points.text: “granting adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue” while the only stated failure is “a request no longer pending refused.”
open_points.question: What happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised, deleted, or becomes unavailable between display and submission?
options: Refuse the answer and leave the request pending
Clear the request but grant nothing
Apply the same project checks as direct grant and define whether clearing is atomic with them
open_points.default_guess: Apply direct-grant checks atomically; on failure, change nothing and leave the request pending.

open_points.subject: Retention-review inputs
open_points.text: “Registry gives that review what it needs” including “the date a project was archived, and the owner's mark that a customer relationship has ended,” but no primary read or list action promises to expose those values or a retention-review view.
open_points.question: Through which concrete action and output can the owner obtain archived dates, relationship-ended dates and current restriction or erasure states for the periodic review?
options: Existing project and customer reads/lists include those values
A dedicated retention-review action returns them
The audit log is the sole source
open_points.default_guess: Include the current retention-relevant state and dates in owner project and customer reads and lists.

open_points.subject: Audit coverage
open_points.text: “only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.”
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries: do room and artifact changes, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, relationship end/resume, imports, refused changes and audit erasure count?
options: The stated list is exhaustive
Every accepted state-changing primary action is audited
Only an explicitly enumerated subset is audited, to be named here
open_points.default_guess: Audit every accepted state-changing primary action plus the required audit-erasure entry, but not ordinary reads or refused calls.

open_points.subject: Audit outcome field
open_points.text: The audit entry includes “the outcome,” while Registry records “only significant changes of state” and excludes ordinary agent calls.
open_points.question: Does the audit log record refused attempts at significant changes, or does `outcome` describe only successful state changes?
options: Only successful changes are logged
Both successful and refused significant mutations are logged
Only selected security-relevant refusals are logged
open_points.default_guess: Log only successful state changes; use `outcome` to describe the resulting state.
